recommendations.description: Launch a TX DSNP HMO acute inpatient policy review for PA-required ER admissions concentrated at BEN TAUB HOSPITAL and other highest-cost acute facilities, targeting Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections with MCC, Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC, Miscellaneous Disorders of Nutrition, Metabolism, and Fluids and Electrolytes with MCC, and Acute Myocardial Infarction, Discharged Alive with MCC, to confirm prior authorization, enforce denials, review UM/P.A.V. criteria for UTI SITE NOT SPECIFIED and ACUTE CYSTITIS WITHOUT HEMATURIA admissions, and verify claims are processing per contractual reimbursement obligations with site-of-care or contract remediation action.
evidence: TX DSNP acute hospital utilization added $48.3M with 2,169 more admissions.
Kidney/UTI with MCC paid per admit rose about $9.2K.
Metabolic/electrolyte DRGs paid per admit rose about $2.7K.
UTI SITE NOT SPECIFIED added $1.1M on 96 admissions.
ACUTE CYSTITIS WITHOUT HEMATURIA added $0.5M.

recommendations.description: Audit TX AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION PA mapping by reconciling prior-auth-required Y/N buckets to paid inpatient claims and denial enforcement, and review claims processing/reprocessing for BEN TAUB HOSPITAL DSNP HMO acute ER admits, prioritizing Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections with MCC before any UM or reimbursement policy change.
evidence: TX AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION accounts for about $44.1M of movement.
Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections with MCC adds about $151K.
Pattern flags auth_or_mapping_shift and requires_validation_before_action.
Largest affected context includes BEN TAUB HOSPITAL, DSNP HMO, acute hospital, ER admits.
Business terms include auth-to-claim validation and coding validation.
peer_benchmarking: BCBS_TX excludes asymptomatic urinary screening, prostate biopsy assessment, and post-resolution follow-up cultures.
Centene limits asymptomatic bacteriuria coverage and denies molecular or multiplex UTI panels.
Humana denies routine general encounter primary diagnoses without abnormal findings.

recommendations.description: Initiate a TX inpatient claims and contract remediation review for PA-required DSNP HMO Not Mapped claims and DSNP HMO/CSNP HMO Physical Rehab claims at TEXAS REHABILITATION HOSPITAL OF FORT WORT, including authorization-to-actual matching, payment reprocessing where contract logic failed, and site-of-care review for higher-cost utilization.
evidence: TX DSNP HMO Not Mapped spend increased $8.3M across 190 admissions.
Not Mapped paid per admit increased about $31.6K.
Physical Rehab pressure includes TEXAS REHABILITATION HOSPITAL OF FORT WORT.
All component groups have PA required indicator Y.
peer_benchmarking: Humana: No site-of-care restrictions stated in provided policy summary.

recommendations.description: Implement a VA PA-required acute-hospital inpatient exception review for Acute Myocardial Infarction, Discharged Alive with MCC; Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections with and without MCC; Miscellaneous Disorders of Nutrition, Metabolism, and Fluids and Electrolytes with MCC; and Esophagitis, Gastroenteritis and Miscellaneous Digestive Disorders without MCC across impacted DSNP HMO, CSNP HMO, and Medicare HMO lines, confirming prior authorization, comparing provider paid-per-admit for SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL and other named facilities, and escalating outlier units for site-of-care, contract compliance, and contract remediation review.
evidence: HTN HRT CKD W/HF STAGE 1-4/UNS CKD leads AMI with MCC growth.
FLUID OVERLOAD UNSPECIFIED and HYPERKALEMIA drive metabolic-electrolyte MCC admissions.
Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections with MCC shows mixed volume and unit-cost pressure.
PA-required acute hospital claims recur across DSNP HMO, CSNP HMO, and Medicare HMO.
SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL appears on a leading AMI with MCC card.
peer_benchmarking: Humana applies Medicare Advantage criteria and limits CHF and serial troponin testing frequency.

recommendations.description: Hold any IN and VA policy or UM changes tied to AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION until a state- and provider-level auth-to-paid-claim reconciliation and contractual claims-processing review is completed for Acute Myocardial Infarction, Discharged Alive with MCC; Miscellaneous Disorders of Nutrition, Metabolism, and Fluids and Electrolytes with MCC; and Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC.
evidence: Flags show auth_or_mapping_shift and requires_validation_before_action.
IN and VA AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION movement totals about $3.3M.
Largest affected DRGs are AMI with MCC and metabolic-electrolyte with MCC.
Recommended next step is reconcile authorization coding to paid claims.
peer_benchmarking: Humana shows no documented policy mention or auth detail.

recommendations.description: Initiate a targeted DSNP HMO acute inpatient utilization management and prior-authorization enforcement review in VA first, then CT, FL, LA, NJ, TN, and WI, limited to Acute Myocardial Infarction, Discharged Alive with MCC; Miscellaneous Disorders of Nutrition, Metabolism, and Fluids and Electrolytes with MCC; Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections with MCC; and Esophagitis, Gastroenteritis and Miscellaneous Digestive Disorders without MCC, and reconcile authorization records to actual admissions for claims-processing escalation where mismatches are found.
evidence: Recurring DSNP HMO acute hospital growth spans CT, FL, LA, NJ, TN, VA, and WI.
Pattern is utilization-led, with admissions up and unit cost mixed.
VA contributes most pressure in AMI and metabolic-electrolyte DRGs.
Auth dimension present and business terms flag auth-to-claim validation.
Drill context names Sentara Norfolk General, Ben Taub, and Queens Hospital Center.
peer_benchmarking: Humana summary shows no relevant inpatient DRG adjudication policy for this DSNP acute pattern.

recommendations.description: Initiate a provider-specific contract compliance and claims-processing review for THE CLEVELAND CLINIC FOUNDATION and UHCMC, including auth-to-claim matching and site-of-care validation for Medicare HMO Not Mapped and DSNP HMO acute admissions involving Acute Myocardial Infarction, Discharged Alive with MCC; Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections with MCC; and Cardiac Valve and Other Major Cardiothoracic Procedures without Cardiac Catheterization with MCC.
evidence: OH spend pressure is concentrated in THE CLEVELAND CLINIC FOUNDATION and UHCMC.
Medicare HMO Not Mapped claims drove pressure across both providers.
DSNP HMO acute admissions rose for AMI with MCC.
Kidney/UTI with MCC also contributed to acute inpatient growth.
Invalid facility rows indicate classification weakness in OH site-of-care data.
PA-required claims carry auth-to-claim validation flags.
peer_benchmarking: United Health bundles UB04 hospital facility claims; routine services and supplies are not separate.
Humana bundles and documents restricted independent lab rules for ACS symptoms.

recommendations.description: Open a case-level claims and contract compliance audit for UHCMC, THE CLEVELAND CLINIC FOUNDATION, and KAWEAH DELTA HEALTH CARE inpatient outliers tied to tracheostomy and prolonged mechanical ventilation, Connective Tissue Disorders with MCC, and coronary bypass with MCC; confirm eligibility, contractual adjudication, final-bill status, and zeroed interim or first claims before any broader inpatient policy action.
evidence: UHCMC had a single tracheostomy and prolonged mechanical ventilation admission with ACQUIRED HEMOPHILIA.
THE CLEVELAND CLINIC FOUNDATION had a single Connective Tissue Disorders with MCC admission.
KAWEAH DELTA HEALTH CARE had a single coronary bypass with MCC admission.
Pattern flags include low_volume_run, repeated_delta_concentration, and small_n_admissions.
Validation needed because cases are low-volume and include unattributed admissions.
peer_benchmarking: Cigna notes bundled facility and respiratory reimbursement is off-topic for DRG inpatient outlier adjudication.
Molina bundles routine hospital services and identifies no separate outlier reimbursement approach.
United Health bundles routine UB04 facility services, not catastrophic DRG outlier review.
